Maya R.: ran a neighborhood stress test for the new sem-embed-2 model. Observed ~12% drop in recall@5 on 'silence' queries (very short / punctuation-only). attaching quick numbers.

Kevin T.: can you paste the eval command + dataset?

Maya R.: sure — command:
```
./eval --model sem-embed-2 --dataset silence-holdout --seed 42 --metric recall@k --k 5
```

EmbedEvalBot: job 57843 finished (4m21s) — results uploaded to gs://redwood-evals/silence-neighborhood/1723459999/

Lia Chen: hmmm we've seen a similar pattern on compact variants — short queries collapse to a narrow cone sometimes. could be post-norm issues or quantization bias. :thinking_face:

Maya R.: quick aggregated numbers (holdout):
- sem-embed-1 (baseline, fp16): recall@5 = 0.73
- sem-embed-2 (fp16): recall@5 = 0.68
- sem-embed-2 (int8): recall@5 = 0.61

Evan S.: did you try L2-normalization before indexing? also what batchsize / kv-cache settings?

Maya R.: embeddings L2-normalized for these runs. batchsize=64, kv-cache off. no prefix caching.

Kevin T.: try comparing cosine vs dot after normalization. also dump neighbor distances (k=50) and radius hist to see clustering tightness.

Lia Chen: add silhouette score and cluster purity on the silence subset. if int8 is worse, check per-channel scale quantization and calibration set.

Maya R.: running knn k=50 radius sweep + silhouette. will post plots in this thread when done. likely follow-up tomorrow. link to scratch CSV: internal-only (gs://redwood-evals/scratch/1723459999.csv) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Kevin T.: sounds good. another hypothesis: token-level embedding for punctuation-only queries might map to special tokens — maybe need short-query augmentation in contrastive fine-tuning. @Evan S. @Lia Chen

Maya R.: noted. I'll add short-query augmentation and rerun int8 calibration. thanks all.
